title: Does a strict schema cost quality
statement: Open question: does forcing a strict output schema on a writer buy structural compliance at the cost of quality in its free-text parts?
example: A strict schema made 5 of 5 document-based items structurally valid against 0 of 5 in plain structured-object mode.
detail: On 5 document-based items, schema-constrained output gave 5/5 structural compliance against 0/5 in plain structured-object mode, and the strict mode was deployed (`findings_sftv7_20260424.md`). A research note in the same project cites a study in which three of four models lost 25 to 63 points on a math-reasoning benchmark in JSON mode, and the project's index keeps strict modes off by default for free-form item types (`research_constrained_decoding_per_cell.md`, `MEMORY.md`).
against: Five items only (`findings_sftv7_20260424.md`, line 28). The cited losses are on math reasoning, and the same study found JSON mode helped on a classification task, 41.6% to 60.3% for one model (`research_constrained_decoding_per_cell.md`, line 30).

evidence.quote: JSON mode loses 25-63pp on reasoning tasks; per-cell decision; default OFF for free-form cells.
GSM8K reasoning, same model, same prompts, free-form vs JSON-mode constrained:
Three of four mainstream models lose 25–63pp on a reasoning task in JSON mode.
Same paper shows JSON mode *helps* on classification (Gemini-1.5-Flash 41.6% → 60.3% on DDXPlus). **Direction depends on task.**
*Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models*, EMNLP 2024 Industry Track](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-industry.91/)
